deviations: PROFILE = mock, NOT the real-signet chain the standup brief described. Rationale: (a) none of the 9 PRs touch services/worker/src/chain/, the broadcast path, or RPC integration, so mock exercises 100% of the changed lines; (b) mock (USE_MOCKS=true / anchoring off) is the canonical shared-staging T2 posture; (c) provisioning a real-treasury signet rig is operator-gated (provision-isolated-rig.sh CONFIRM_REAL_CONFIG) and its exact known-good signet wiring could not be verified because the auto-mode classifier blocks reading the frozen signet rigs' env. Real-signet lifecycle is available as an operator-gated follow-up if chain-grade evidence is wanted; it would add no coverage of the changed lines.

Supabase project created via `supabase projects create` (CLI, controlled DB password) instead of MCP create_project, because clean_mirror requires numeric-ledger schema replay via `supabase db push --linked` which needs a known DB password (MCP create_project does not expose one). Cost ($10/mo) acknowledged via MCP get_cost.

Deployed via `gcloud run deploy` on the digest-pinned RC image rather than scripts/staging/deploy.sh, because deploy.sh is hard-scoped to the shared arkova-worker-staging service and cannot target an ad-hoc isolated service.

provision-isolated-rig.sh (the documented orchestrator) was used only for dry-run plan validation, not --apply: its defaults are hardwired for a single-PR T3 chain-resilience soak (driver_path pr1408, tier T3, 2880-min uptime) and its mock profile skips Cloud Scheduler at min-instances=0 - unsuitable for this T2 batch. Standup was done manually to match T2 semantics + wire the changed cron routes.

Soak clock reset once (rev 00001 -> 00002) to load the DB-backed ENABLE_BATCH_ANCHORING switchboard flag (fresh rigs boot with empty switchboard_flags). Same image digest; RC head unchanged; only a flag-reload env marker differs, so exact-head evidence is preserved.
